newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed eases, winter demand supportive.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed eases, winter demand supportive.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe eased 10 marks on the week to 430 marks a tonne free Hamburg buyers but underlying demand will prevent sharp losses, brokers said on Friday.
Price falls in the Chicago soy complex on bearish weather news earlier this week weighed on rapeseed, as did the prospect of an excellent domestic crop.
But processors were also aware of possibly tight oilseeds supply in the 1997/98 season and were looking to build some Nov/Jan cover.
Farmers were locking away supply to await local and export demand.
Rapeseed for the winter months last traded at 460 marks.
Traders said prices could rise after October, when crusher cover in Europe will be thinning, depending on the world market outlook at that stage.
Canada is expected to produce at least six million tonnes after five million last year, but may not meet all the possible global protein shortfalls should U.S. soy exports fall short of expectations.
That would support demand for European rapeseed, also boosted by weak EU currencies versus the dollar.
The European rapeseed harvest has produced large supplies and mixed yields.
Germany's 1997 crop is estimated at 2.7 million tonnes, versus 1.97 million in 1996, while France's could reach 3.2 million (2.9 million in 1996).
German yield forecasts are for 2.94 tonnes per hectare (2.31 in 1996) but French yields may be 10 percent down.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were steady at 430-440 marks while Sept buyers were at 435-440.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures last traded at 450 marks, up two from Thursday's close.
In products, nearby rape meal was steady, but hard to market, and the forward months were sharply lower.
August rape meal was unchanged at 23.50 marks/100 kg with Sept/Oct at 23.25 (24.50) and Nov/Jan at 24.25 (26.50).
Rape oil prices held broadly steady on export demand.
Aug and Sept/Oct oil were at 95.00 marks/100 kg.
